e: RDS Proxy keeps application connections alive and pools them across a database failover, so the application reconnects quickly and failover downtime drops substantially, with little operational work. More replicas, a secondary cluster, or Memcached don't shorten failover.

Deploying the web and application tiers in a second Region, using an Aurora global database across both Regions, and Route 53 health checks with failover routing (promoting the secondary as needed) gives the most fault tolerance and minimal downtime. Auto Scaling groups can't span Regions, and DMS or standard cross-Region replicas are slower or less managed.

AWS Transfer Family provides a managed FTP endpoint (no client changes) that stores files in S3, and an S3 event triggers a Lambda function to process each file as soon as it arrives and then delete it. Each file takes 3 to 8 minutes, within Lambda's 15-minute limit. EC2 FTP servers, Glacier, or nightly batch runs are slower and need more management.

Amazon RDS is a managed database service that removes patching and administration, and encryption at rest (KMS) protects the sensitive data. EC2-hosted databases keep the operational burden, Macie is for S3, and CloudWatch Logs isn't data protection.

Global Accelerator supports TCP and UDP listeners and routes players over the AWS global network to the best NLB endpoint, improving performance and cutting latency. CloudFront and ALBs don't handle UDP game traffic, and API Gateway isn't for TCP/UDP gaming.

A Lambda function URL gives the function a dedicated HTTPS endpoint that the third party can call directly, with no extra services to manage. ALB adds cost and setup, and SNS or SQS hostnames can't receive arbitrary webhooks.

Register the domain with a wildcard custom domain record in Route 53 pointing to API Gateway, request a wildcard ACM certificate in the same Region as the API (a Regional API endpoint uses a certificate from its own Region), and create the custom domain name in API Gateway using that certificate. That gives each customer its own secure URL without per-customer hosted zones or APIs.

Amazon Macie automatically discovers PII in S3 and publishes findings to EventBridge, and a rule matching the sensitive data finding type can notify the security team through SNS (a notification service). GuardDuty doesn't detect PII, and SQS isn't a notification channel for people.

Keep logs in S3 Standard for the first 30 days of frequent analysis, then transition to Standard-IA (still highly available) for the backup period, and expire at 90 days. Moving to Glacier at day 90 has no cost effect before deletion, and Glacier after 30 days or One Zone-IA lose the availability requirement or frequent analysis. Option B best matches availability and cost.

EKS supports envelope encryption of Kubernetes secrets in etcd using a KMS key, enabled on the cluster (KMS secrets encryption). Secrets Manager doesn't encrypt etcd, and EBS encryption covers volumes, not etcd secrets.

A Multi-AZ DB cluster has two readable standby instances with a reader endpoint, giving high availability and a place for the data scientists' complex queries without hitting the writer, at lower cost than adding separate read replicas to a Multi-AZ instance. A Multi-AZ instance standby can't be read.

RDS for MySQL as a Multi-AZ DB cluster gives high availability across three AZs with read capacity, ElastiCache for Redis with high availability stores sessions and caches reads (Redis offers persistence and replication, unlike Memcached), and an Auto Scaling group across three AZs absorbs traffic spikes. A single-AZ database isn't highly available, and DynamoDB would require rewriting the application.

CloudFront geographic restrictions with an allow list let the company serve content only to viewers in the approved countries and show a custom error to others, and the list can be updated as the rollout expands. Signed URLs, encryption, or time limits don't restrict by country.

AWS Elastic Disaster Recovery continuously replicates disk changes to low-cost staging resources on AWS (pilot light), meeting a 30-second RPO and a 60-minute RTO while minimizing cost. Always On active/active on Enterprise is expensive, DMS to RDS warm standby costs more, and nightly backups can't meet a 30-second RPO.

RDS for Oracle in a Multi-AZ configuration provides higher availability, and the reader instance in the cluster deployment can serve reporting. A Single-AZ deployment lacks availability, and Aurora isn't Oracle and can't be created from an RDS Multi-AZ instance. Option C is the answer given the choices.

A serverless design is cheapest for idle, unpredictable traffic: API Gateway with Lambda and DynamoDB for the backend, a Cognito user pool to authenticate subscribed users, and Amplify (with integrated CloudFront) to serve the frontend. ECS with ALB and RDS cost more when idle, identity pools don't authenticate users themselves, and S3 static hosting can't run PHP.

CloudFront signed URLs restrict access to specific files for premium customers and are well suited to on-demand, per-file access such as movie rentals or music downloads, and they can carry expirations. S3 signed cookies don't exist, OAC restricts origin access rather than viewers, and field-level encryption protects form data.

Savings Plan discounts apply across accounts in an organization when discount sharing is enabled in the management account's billing preferences. In the question's arrangement (with an organization), the Savings Plan can be shared with other accounts through the organization (using RAM sharing for the plan). Options B, D, and E don't correctly enable sharing.

A canary release deployment sends a percentage of traffic to the new API version while production keeps serving the rest, so you can verify it and then promote it with minimal customer impact and no data loss. Overwriting or merging definitions or switching domains affects all traffic at once.

A Route 53 active-passive failover configuration with a health check on the ALB sends traffic to a static error page hosted in S3 when the ALB is unhealthy, with minimal changes and no extra servers. Latency, multivalue, or EC2-hosted pages add complexity or don't fail over as described.

A Storage Gateway Tape Gateway presents an iSCSI virtual tape library to existing backup applications, so the company eliminates physical tapes while keeping its backup software and workflows. NFS or EFS interfaces don't present virtual tapes.

Kinesis Data Firehose is a fully managed service that ingests high-volume streaming data and delivers it to S3 in near real time with automatic scaling and no servers, the least operational overhead. Glue, Lambda, or DMS aren't built for this ingestion pattern.

Grouping the accounts into OUs in AWS Organizations and attaching service control policies lets the company centrally allow or deny which services each department's accounts can use, with little operational work. Systems Manager, CloudFormation, and Service Catalog don't enforce service restrictions account-wide.

A NAT gateway in a public subnet, with the private subnet route table sending internet-bound traffic to it, lets the private MySQL instances make outbound requests while remaining unreachable from the internet, and it's managed with no operational overhead. NAT instances need maintenance, and routing private subnets to an internet gateway would expose them.

To decrypt environment variables, the Lambda execution role needs KMS permissions (such as kms:Decrypt), and the KMS key policy must allow that role to use the key. Resource or function policies control who can invoke the function, not what it can access.
